topic: Blood transfusion and cross-matching in arthroplasty
usual_baseline: Too much blood ordered and given. THR cross-match to transfusion ratio 3.21 [1213]; spine 4.4:1 and 16.6:1 [1275, 1215]. MSBOS compliance 52%, over-crossmatching 43% [1549]. 46% of THR transfusions inappropriate [1258], 24% in another unit [1575]. Blood loss recorded in only 57% of operations [1181]. 67% of transfused THR patients got two units [1233].
fix_that_works: Stopping routine cross-match for THR, with a day 2 full blood count: units cross-matched but not transfused fell 96%, C:T ratio 3.21 to 1.62 [1213]. A spine-specific guideline raised MSBOS compliance from 52% to 72% and cut over-crossmatching from 43% to 12% [1549]. A new agreed tariff cut the C:T ratio from 16.6:1 to 11.5:1 [1215].
fix_that_fails: Staff education and amendments to the local transfusion policy gave no reduction in transfusion rates after primary THR [1258].
consultant_advice: Cross-match ordering has largely been fixed; 73% of hospitals already use group-and-save [1233]. Audit whether each transfusion met a haemoglobin trigger and whether single units were used. Pre-operative anaemia is more useful: 15% had Hb below 12 g/dl and 57% of them were transfused [1233].
